ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, point P is located 22.5cm directly above the bottom end Q of an inclined plane with an inclination angle of 37°. Now a smooth inclined straight track is built from point P toward the inclined plane, so that a small block starts from rest at point P and slides along this track to the inclined plane, with g taken as 10m/s^2. What is the shortest time for the small block to slide to the inclined plane?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal ground line, whose right end is point Q; from Q an inclined plane extends upward to the left, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal line is marked as 37°; point P is directly above Q, and the segment between P and Q is represented by a vertical dashed line; the problem statement gives PQ=22.5 cm. The small block starts from P and reaches a certain point on the inclined plane along an artificially built smooth inclined straight track. Reasoning: Take Q as the coordinate origin, vertically upward as the y-axis, and horizontally rightward as the x-axis. Let h=PQ=22.5 cm=0.225 m, then P=(0,h). Let the track endpoint A be on the inclined plane, and let the distance of A relative to Q along the inclined plane upward to the left be s, then A=(-s cos37°, s sin37°). The vertical descent from P to A is Δy=h-s sin37°, and the square of the track length is L^2=(s cos37°)^2+(h-s sin37°)^2. The block starts from rest and does uniformly accelerated motion along the smooth straight track; the descent height at the end is Δy, and the acceleration along the track is gΔy/L, so L=1/2·(gΔy/L)t^2, giving t^2=2L^2/(gΔy). Let u=Δy, then the height of point A is h-u, so the magnitude of the horizontal displacement corresponding to the inclined plane is (h-u)cot37°, hence L^2=u^2+(h-u)^2cot^2 37°. To make the time shortest, that is, minimize F=L^2/u. Differentiating F gives the optimum at u=h cos37°. Taking cos37°=0.8 and sin37°=0.6, then u=0.225×0.8=0.18 m. At this time L^2/u=0.2 m, so t^2=2×0.2/10=0.04, t=0.2 s.
